idiom_name: wrapper struct embedding the target interface + http middleware func(next http.Handler)
implementation_notes: Go replaces the interceptor object with a wrapper struct that embeds the target interface and overrides only the audited methods - the embedded field supplies forwarding for everything else, so the classic Interceptor/InvocationContext structure disappears into a single type definition. On the HTTP side the same idea is a middleware function, func(next http.Handler) http.Handler, which records the request and the response status around next.ServeHTTP. There is no container and no annotation: enrolment happens explicitly at wiring time, and calls made on the concrete type or from inside the target bypass the wrapper - so the wrapper must be the only value callers receive.
pitfalls: Embedding copies the interface value: keep the sink reference immutable and use pointer receivers if the wrapper carries state (a copied struct with a mutex is a bug).
Embedding the concrete type instead of the interface exposes the unwrapped implementation to callers through type assertions or direct field use.
A method that is not overridden forwards silently, so the auditor must confirm the method set rather than assume the embedding audits everything.
